explain.say: A heat pump works like a fridge in reverse. Outside, a fan blows air over pipes holding a refrigerant so cold that even winter air is warmer, so heat flows into it and the refrigerant boils into a gas.

faq.q: How can a heat pump get heat from cold air?
faq.a: Even air at minus 10 degrees Celsius contains heat energy. The refrigerant outside is made colder still, so heat flows from the air into it, because heat always flows from warmer to colder.
asks: Does a heat pump work below freezing?

faq.q: What does the compressor do in a heat pump?
faq.a: It squeezes the refrigerant gas into a smaller space, raising its pressure and temperature. That lifts the heat collected outside to a temperature useful for heating a home. It is the part that uses electricity.
asks: Why does a heat pump need electricity?

faq.q: What does the expansion valve do?
faq.a: It is a narrow opening that the liquid refrigerant squeezes through. Its pressure drops suddenly, which makes it very cold, ready to absorb heat outside again.
asks: Why does the refrigerant get cold?

faq.q: Is a heat pump the same as a fridge?
faq.a: It uses the same cycle. A fridge pumps heat out of its cold box into your kitchen; a heat pump pumps heat out of the cold outdoors into your home. Many heat pumps can also run in reverse to cool.
asks: Can a heat pump cool a house?

faq.q: Do heat pumps work in winter?
faq.a: Yes. Modern air source heat pumps work well below freezing and are common in cold countries like Norway and Sweden. Their efficiency drops a little as it gets colder.
asks: Are heat pumps good in cold countries?

facts: Heat pumps use the same refrigeration cycle as fridges, but deliver the heat into the home.
Norway has one of the highest numbers of heat pumps per household in the world.

quiz.say: Which part of a heat pump uses electricity to raise the refrigerant's temperature?
quiz.why: The compressor squeezes the gas, raising its pressure and temperature, and it runs on electricity.

wrong.1: The expansion valve lowers the pressure, making the refrigerant cold.
wrong.2: The outdoor air supplies heat, but it does not raise the temperature.
